# Installed host field audit, 2026-10-19

`installed-contract.json` contains source-derived feature reproductions from
WorkBuddy 5.3.8's installed `codebuddy.js` constructors/serializers and Loomy
0.9.39's hash-matched OpenCode source map. WorkBuddy messages were produced by
the installed `itemsToMessages` and content normalization functions, using
synthetic values shaped by the observed producers. These entries are source
reproductions, not literal wire captures.

The two `loomy-installed-cli-turn-*` entries are sanitized literal HTTP requests from the installed
Loomy OpenCode executable. It ran with a fresh HOME/config/workspace, disabled
default/external plugins, updates, external skills and model fetching. A local
mock provider requested a read of a synthetic file, then returned the final
marker. Runtime prompt strings, tool argument values, results and identities
were replaced consistently; protocol fields, schemas and JSON types remain.
No live host task, login or credential was used.

The installed OpenCode executable and the executable beside the source map
both have SHA256
`e3d5f71df3fffa86ab698a36ef7c0cb36e3d69edb0efc33f83a62626a0fec3fb`.
The compatible SDK is bundled in the source map; the default integration uses
`@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`, with no assumption about the meaning of arbitrary
Provider options. `promptCacheKey` and `reasoningSummary` retain their literal
source-emitted spelling on native Chat.

Regression checks cover field/type/role boundaries, routing normalization,
native request preservation, zero outbound work for lossy conversion, metadata
privacy scanning, and both application HTTP routes with JSON/SSE and routing
enabled/disabled/unavailable. These checks do not establish media support,
every upstream vendor's support for every control, or future host versions.

## WorkBuddy 5.8.3 follow-up audit, 2026-10-28

The additional `workbuddy-5.8.3-*` cases were generated by executing the installed
`itemsToMessages`, `extractAllUserContent`, `extractAllAssistantContent` and
tool-result normalization functions, extracted without modification from the
installed lazy chunk. Inputs use synthetic values shaped by the installed
producers; these are serializer executions, not captured requests or proof that
every producer survives the client's earlier filtering. The original fixtures
remain intact.

Source SHA256:

- `codebuddy-lite-wb.mjs`:
  `92899eb4b9d9403a95ceae17dc95e6816bb28dd9fe099790240b5b54d1dac330`
- `lazy-lite-wb/4354.f4e1e1f7.mjs`:
  `b4248ce4c4ec43d56bdbe973110ca107fc6193b51d8f453549f0cae190f41c92`

The serializer spreads user/system/assistant message `providerData` directly
into Chat messages, copies function-call metadata onto assistant messages, and
copies function-result metadata onto tool messages. The audited producers cover
new user turns and steering, subagent request identity, scheduled tasks,
follow-up queue IDs/timestamps, abort markers, summary normalization, content
filter notices, hook blocking details and runtime security, mod logs, workflow
source, approval UI metadata, and final/streaming/injected/stopped tool history.
It also covers user command-output goal status, typed text attachment references,
and model-builder thinking budgets and growth-event extras. Attachment reference
objects remain opaque metadata next to text; no file is read by these tests.
Each case names its source. Combined user/tool/continuation history verifies
that opening a new turn and continuing after a tool retain their different
boolean values and correlation IDs. Empty IDs, empty hook arrays and fractional
timestamps exercise emitted/default value shapes as well as populated values.

Before the registry change, the existing
`TestInstalledHostFieldContractAcrossValidationRoutingAndNativeCloud` failed
with `unsupported or invalid model input` on the new prompt, request identity,
queue, hook and tool-history cases. The same fixture matrix also runs through
privacy preparation and real loopback HTTP in direct, cloud-judgment and
unavailable-judgment modes with JSON/SSE, without contacting a vendor or reading
live host settings. Cross-protocol conversion keeps its explicit zero-attempt
capability error when destination codecs cannot preserve these fields.

## WorkBuddy completed-turn step sequence audit, 2026-10-28

The `workbuddy-5.8.3-*-step-seq` cases execute the same hash-matched installed
`providerDataOf`, `itemsToMessages` and content normalization functions with
synthetic messages and identities. `withModelMessageCorrelation` stamps
`messageId`, `conversationRequestId` and `stepSeq` onto model output, including
function calls; saved tool results also carry this correlation. The sequence
starts at zero and advances for main-loop model calls. Ordinary completed-turn,
tool continuation and zero-step auxiliary histories are separate cases. Their
normalized `usage` includes the array detail shapes emitted by the installed
client. These are serializer reproductions, not captured HTTP requests.

Before adding `stepSeq` to the shared registry, all three cases fail native
cloud validation with `unsupported or invalid model input`; the existing
completed-turn `usage` regression already passes. The common fixture matrix
also exercises routing, privacy, native forwarding, cross-protocol refusal,
and direct/routed loopback HTTP with JSON/SSE. This does not establish support
in an installed release or a real cloud conversation.
